info.description:
The Oppulse AI backend: the versioned HTTP contract the frontend speaks, the
agent that researches opportunities and explains what it found, and the
deterministic services that decide what the agent may conclude.
info.title: Oppulse AI

get.description: The alerts in the student's app.

post.description: Marks an alert as read.

Retries a delivery.

Only the in-app channel is active, and an in-app alert cannot fail its
own delivery, so there is nothing to retry. The endpoint says so rather
than pretending to have sent something.

get.description: The caller's applications.
One application.

patch.description: Changes an application's status, its notes or its tasks.

get.description: The documents prepared for one application.

post.description:
Starts a document for an application.

It is a starting point grounded in the confirmed facts, and it is never
applied without the student.

Runs an action the assistant offered.

Everything that creates state is confirmed by the student first: the
interface asks, and only then does this endpoint run.

get.description:
The conversation.

The frontend keeps a copy so a refresh is instant; this is the copy that
decides what a turn may use.

post.description:
Asks the assistant something.

The context is assembled here, and only here: the client says *what* it
selected, and the service decides what may be read.

Sends a verification link.

The token comes back in the response because the prototype cannot
deliver email yet. In the backend it only ever travels in the message.

Confirms the address.

Only the backend can set this. The client cannot ask for a verified
address, and no sensitive alert is sent to an unverified one.

Asks for a password reset link.

The answer is the same whether or not the address has an account: the
endpoint must never confirm who has one, or it becomes a way of
discovering who is using the product.

Sets a new password with a reset token.

The token is single-use, and every session of that account is revoked:
a password reset is how an account is recovered, so the old sessions
must not survive it.

get.description:
The current session.

When the access token has expired but the refresh token is still good,
the session is renewed here — which is why the frontend's contract
carries no token at all: it asks for the session and gets one.

post.description:
Signs a student in.

The failure message is the same whether the address is unknown or the
password is wrong: the endpoint must not confirm which addresses have
accounts.
Signs the student out, everywhere.
Creates an account.

get.description: What is connected, per service.
The caller's documents.

post.description:
Uploads a document.

The file is read here, on our own machine. Only the text of the pages we
could read is ever sent to a model provider, and the pages we could not
read are named.

delete.description:
Deletes a document.

The facts extracted from it are withdrawn, unless the student confirmed
them separately.

get.description: One document.

patch.description:
Changes the consent, or the category.

The consent is the student's decision about whether this document may be
used as AI context, and it is revocable at any time.

get.description: Downloads the caller's private document bytes.
One document.

patch.description:
Saves an edit as a new version.

The previous version stays recoverable, and a stale edit is refused
rather than silently overwriting someone else's work.

post.description:
Asks the assistant to propose a revision.

The proposal is a *proposal*: it does not touch the document, and the
student reviews the diff before accepting it.

Accepts a proposal, as a new version.

The previous version stays recoverable, and the acceptance is recorded.
Discards a proposal. The document is unchanged.

get.description: Every version of a document, oldest first.

schema.title: Response List Draft Versions Api V1 Drafts  Id  Versions Get

get.description: The caller's missions.

post.description: Creates a mission.

get.description: One mission.

post.description:
Queues a run.

A run is a row with a lease, so a refresh neither loses it nor starts a
second one: an unfinished run for this mission is resumed instead. With
an `Idempotency-Key`, the same key always names the same run — even
after that run finished — because the key is stored on the run itself
and the unique constraint makes the claim atomic.

get.description: The changes the agent noticed.
The sources the student is watching.

post.description: Starts watching a source.

patch.description: Pauses, resumes or re-times a watched source.

get.description:
The one action the student should take next.

It is derived, not authored: the same inputs always produce the same
recommendation, and it is always tied to a real blocker.

post.description:
Turns the answers into a mission, and starts the run.

The date of birth goes to the **protected** section — never into a fact,
never into the mission — because it is used for one thing only.

get.description: The student's draft.

put.description:
Saves the draft.

Every answer is saved as it is given, so a refresh — or a lost
connection — never costs the student their answers.

get.description: The opportunities, ranked against the confirmed profile.

post.description:
Analyses a link without saving a mission first.

It starts a research run, and the run is durable: the browser may close
and the run continues.

schema.title: Response Analyze Opportunity Api V1 Opportunities Analyze Post

post.description:
Compares two to four opportunities side by side.

It is a read of what the agent already found: the same eligibility,
funding and deadline, with the differences named. It never invents a
ranking the evidence does not support.

get.description: One opportunity, with its evidence and its sources.

post.description:
Turns a saved opportunity into a workspace.

The checklist is drawn from the call, and it is the same checklist the
assistant offers — so the student sees one list, not two.

schema.title: Response Create Application Api V1 Opportunities  Id  Applications Post

post.description: Hides an opportunity from the student's list.
Saves an opportunity to the student's plan.

get.description: The caller's profile.

patch.description: Changes the name, the preferences or the consent.

Confirms, corrects, rejects or excludes one fact.

It is not just a write: it changes what the agent can conclude, so every
opportunity is re-evaluated and the history is recorded.

get.description: What each fact is holding up.

The protected section.

It is a separate endpoint on purpose: a routine profile read never
returns the date of birth, so it cannot leak into a list view, a log or
a prompt.

patch.description:
Changes the date of birth, or withdraws it.

Changing it re-evaluates every opportunity, because the age
requirements change with it.

get.description: Every change the student made, newest first.
The profile as it was when the last run started.
One run.

post.description:
Cancels a run.

The run stops at its next checkpoint, and it is not deleted: the student
can see what it did before it stopped.

get.description:
The factual events of a run.

What happened, the object it happened to, and when. Never the model's
internal reasoning.

post.description:
Pauses a run.

The worker stops at its next checkpoint and keeps everything it has
already done; the run stays on the row, so resuming continues from the
stage it paused on rather than starting again.

Re-queues a paused run.

Nothing is re-done: the worker picks the run up and enters at the
stage the checkpoint names.

Re-queues a run that failed or stopped short.

Only the stage that failed is redone: the checkpoint holds what the
earlier stages produced, and their events are already on the timeline.

get.description:
Liveness.

It says "alive" and nothing more. A health check that leaks a version or
a dependency's state is a reconnaissance gift.

Readiness.

The body states which dependencies are ready, so a deployment can be
debugged without a log dive. It never states *why* one is not ready in
terms that could leak a connection string or a key.
